summary: A person brought an asham taluy and then found out he never sinned. What happens to the animal depends on when he found out; Rabbi Meir, the Sages, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yosei explain.

chunks.en: One who brings an asham taluy and then finds out
chunks.st: In the case of one who brings a provisional guilt offering due to uncertainty as to whether he sinned, and it became known to him

chunks.en: that he did not sin:
chunks.st: that he did not sin,

chunks.en: if it was before it was shechted,
chunks.st: if he made that discovery before the ram was slaughtered,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall emerge and graze with the flock
chunks.stMore: as a non-sacred animal, since its consecration was in error.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:
chunks.stMore: Its status is not that of a non-sacred animal; rather it is that of a guilt offering that was disqualified for sacrifice.

chunks.en: it grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: Therefore, it shall graze until it becomes blemished;

words.note: A mum is a blemish that makes an animal unfit for a korban.

chunks.en: then it is sold, and its money goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: and then it shall be sold, and the money received for it shall be allocated for the purchase of communal gift offerings by the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: יִקְרַב, שֶׁאִם אֵינוֹ בָא עַל חֵטְא זֶה,
chunks.en: it is brought as a korban, because if it does not come for this sin,
chunks.st: It shall be sacrificed as a provisional guilt offering, as if it does not come to atone for this sin that he initially thought,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי הוּא בָא עַל חֵטְא אַחֵר.
chunks.en: it comes for another sin.
chunks.st: it comes to atone for another sin of which he is unaware.

chunks.en: If he found out after it was shechted,
chunks.st: If it became known to him that he did not sin after the ram was slaughtered and its blood collected in a container,

chunks.he: הַדָּם יִשָּׁפֵךְ וְהַבָּשָׂר יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵפָה.
chunks.en: the blood is spilled out, and the meat goes out to be burned.
chunks.st: the blood shall be poured into the canal that flows through the Temple courtyard, and the flesh shall go out to the place of burning,
chunks.stMore: like any disqualified offering.

chunks.en: If the blood was already sprinkled,
chunks.st: If the blood was sprinkled
chunks.stMore: before he discovered that he did not sin, and the meat is intact,

chunks.en: the meat may be eaten.
chunks.st: the meat may be eaten
chunks.stMore: by the priests like any other sin offering, as from the moment that its blood was sprinkled the meat is permitted to the priests.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even if the blood is still in the cup,
chunks.st: Even if the blood was still in the cup
chunks.stMore: when he discovered that he did not sin,

chunks.en: it is sprinkled, and the meat may be eaten.
chunks.st: the blood shall be sprinkled and the meat may be eaten.

summary: A sure asham, an ox that is to be stoned, and an eglah arufah are different from an asham taluy. This mishnah explains what happens to each one when it turns out it was not needed.

chunks.en: A sure asham is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of a definite guilt offering, it is not so,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the halakha is different than with regard to a provisional guilt offering.

chunks.en: If it was before it was shechted,
chunks.st: If he made the discovery that he did not sin before the ram was slaughtered,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock,
chunks.stMore: as it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: Once it was shechted, it must be buried.
chunks.st: If it became known to him that he did not sin after the ram was slaughtered, it shall be buried
chunks.stMore: like a non-sacred animal that was slaughtered in the Temple courtyard, and its blood is poured.

chunks.en: If the blood was sprinkled,
chunks.st: If he discovered that he did not sin after the blood was sprinkled,

chunks.en: the meat goes out to be burned.
chunks.st: the flesh shall go out to the place of burning,
chunks.stMore: like any disqualified offering.

chunks.en: An ox that is to be stoned is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of an ox that is sentenced to be stoned (see Exodus 21:28–32), e.g., for killing a person, it is not so,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it also does not have the same halakhic status as a provisional guilt offering.

chunks.en: If it was found out before it was stoned,
chunks.st: If it is discovered that the testimony with regard to the ox was false before it was stoned,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock
chunks.stMore: as it never had the status of an ox sentenced to be stoned.

chunks.en: Once it was stoned, one may benefit from it.
chunks.st: If this was discovered after the ox was stoned, its halakhic status is as though it had not been sentenced, and therefore deriving benefit from its carcass is permitted.

chunks.en: An eglah arufah is not like this.
chunks.st: In the case of a heifer whose neck is broken, when a corpse is found between two cities and the identity of the murderer is unknown (see Deuteronomy 21:1–9), it is not so
chunks.stMore: i.e., the halakha is different than with regard to a provisional guilt offering.

words.note: The eglah arufah is brought when a killed person is found and no one knows who did it.

chunks.en: If it was found out before its neck was broken,
chunks.st: If the identity of the murderer is discovered before the heifer’s neck was broken,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock,
chunks.stMore: as it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: Once its neck was broken, it is buried in its place,
chunks.st: But if the identity of the murderer was discovered after the heifer’s neck was broken, it shall be buried in its place,
chunks.stMore: like any other heifer whose neck is broken.

chunks.en: because from the start it came for a doubt,
chunks.st: The reason is that from the outset the heifer whose neck is broken comes to atone for a situation of uncertainty.
chunks.stMore: Once its neck was broken before the identity of the murderer was revealed, its mitzva was fulfilled,

chunks.en: it atoned for its doubt, and that is done.
chunks.st: as it atoned for its uncertainty and that uncertainty is gone.

summary: Rabbi Eliezer says a person may bring an asham taluy as a gift any day. Bava ben Buta did this every day except the day after Yom Kippur. The Sages say it is brought only for a real doubt.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: A person may give an asham taluy as a gift every
chunks.st: A person may volunteer to bring a provisional guilt offering

chunks.en: day and at any time he wants,
chunks.st: every day and at any time that he chooses,
chunks.stMore: even if there is no uncertainty as to whether he sinned,

chunks.en: and it is called "the asham of chassidim."
chunks.st: and this type of offering was called the guilt offering of the pious,
chunks.stMore: as they brought it due to their constant concern that they might have sinned.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל בָּבָא בֶן בּוּטִי,
chunks.en: They said about Bava ben Buti
chunks.st: They said about Bava ben Buta

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיָה מִתְנַדֵּב אָשָׁם תָּלוּי בְּכָל יוֹם,
chunks.en: that he gave an asham taluy as a gift every day,
chunks.st: that he would volunteer to bring a provisional guilt offering every day

chunks.he: חוּץ מֵאַחַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים יוֹם אֶחָד.
chunks.en: except for one day, the day after Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: except for one day after Yom Kippur,
chunks.stMore: when he would not bring the offering.

chunks.en: He said, "I swear by this house of Hashem,
chunks.st: Bava ben Buta said: I take an oath by this abode of the Divine Presence

chunks.en: if they had let me,
chunks.st: that if they would have allowed me,

chunks.en: I would bring one.
chunks.st: I would have brought a guilt offering even on that day.

chunks.en: But they tell me,
chunks.st: But they would say to me:

chunks.en: 'Wait until you come into a doubt.'"
chunks.st: Wait until you enter into a situation of potential uncertainty.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵין מְבִיאִים אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶלָּא עַל
chunks.en: one brings an asham taluy only for
chunks.st: One brings a provisional guilt offering only

chunks.en: a sin that gets kares when done on purpose and a chatas when done by mistake.
chunks.st: in a case where there is uncertainty as to whether he performed a sin for whose intentional performance one is liable to receive karet and for whose unwitting performance one is liable to bring a sin offering.

summary: After Yom Kippur, a person still must bring a chatas or a sure asham he owes, but not an asham taluy, because Yom Kippur atones for doubts.

chunks.en: Those who must bring chataos and sure ashamos,
chunks.st: Those liable to bring sin offerings and definite guilt offerings

chunks.en: when Yom Kippur has passed,
chunks.st: for whom Yom Kippur has passed

chunks.en: must still bring them after Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: are liable to bring them after Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: Those who must bring an asham taluy
chunks.st: By contrast, those liable to bring provisional guilt offerings

chunks.en: are free. One who has
chunks.st: are exempt from bringing them after Yom Kippur. With regard to one who encountered

chunks.en: a doubt whether he sinned on Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: uncertainty as to whether he performed a sin on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: even at nightfall,
chunks.st: even if it was at nightfall at the end of the day,

chunks.en: is free, because the whole day atones.
chunks.st: he is exempt, as the entire day atones for uncertain sins.

summary: A woman who must bring a bird chatas because of a doubt still brings it after Yom Kippur, because she needs it to eat from korbanos.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלֶיהָ חַטַּאת הָעוֹף סָפֵק,
chunks.en: A woman who must bring a bird chatas because of a doubt,
chunks.st: A woman upon whom it is incumbent to bring a bird sin offering due to uncertainty,
chunks.stMore: e.g., uncertainty with regard to whether or not her miscarriage obligated her to bring the sin offering of a woman who gave birth,

chunks.en: when Yom Kippur has passed,
chunks.st: for whom Yom Kippur has passed,

chunks.en: must still bring it after Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: is liable to bring it after Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: because it lets her eat from korbanos.
chunks.st: This is because the offering does not come as atonement for a sin; rather, it renders her eligible to partake of the meat of offerings.

chunks.en: A bird chatas that comes because of a doubt,
chunks.st: With regard to this bird sin offering that is brought due to uncertainty,

chunks.en: if she found out after its neck was pinched,
chunks.st: if it became known to her that she was exempt from bringing the offering after the nape of the neck of the bird was pinched,

chunks.en: it must be buried.
chunks.st: the bird must be buried.

summary: A person set aside two sela'im for an asham and bought two rams with them. What happens to each ram depends on what he bought them for and how much each is worth.

chunks.en: One who set aside two sela'im for an asham and bought
chunks.st: With regard to one who designates two sela, which is the minimal value of a guilt offering, to purchase a ram for a guilt offering, and he purchased

chunks.en: two rams with them for an asham:
chunks.st: two rams for a guilt offering with the two sela,

chunks.en: if one of them
chunks.st: if one of them is

chunks.en: is worth two sela'im,
chunks.st: now worth two sela,

chunks.en: it is brought for his asham,
chunks.st: he shall sacrifice it for his guilt offering.

chunks.en: and the second one grazes until it gets a mum,
chunks.st: And the second ram that he purchased with the money he designated does not become non-sacred. Rather, it shall graze until it becomes blemished;

chunks.en: then it is sold, and its money goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: and then it shall be sold, and the money received for it shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

chunks.en: If he bought two rams with them for regular use,
chunks.explain: He used holy money, so he did me'ilah.
chunks.st: If he purchased two rams for non-sacred use with those two sela designated for a guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: he has misused consecrated property. He is therefore liable to bring a guilt offering and to compensate the Temple treasury for those two sela and add one-fifth to the sum for a total of ten dinars, as there are four dinars in a sela.

chunks.en: one worth two sela'im
chunks.st: If one of the rams is now worth two sela,

chunks.en: and one worth ten zuz,
chunks.st: and the other one is now worth ten dinars, i.e., two and a half sela,

words.note: A zuz is a silver coin; four zuz make a sela.

chunks.en: the one worth two sela'im is brought for his asham,
chunks.st: the one that is worth two sela shall be sacrificed as his guilt offering for misuse of the two sela,

chunks.en: and the second one for his me'ilah.
chunks.st: and the second one shall be sacrificed for his initial misuse,
chunks.stMore: as it is worth two sela plus one-fifth.

chunks.en: If he bought one for an asham and one for regular use,
chunks.st: In a case where he purchased two rams with those two sela designated for a guilt offering, one for a guilt offering and one for non-sacred use,

chunks.en: if the one for the asham
chunks.st: if the ram for the guilt offering is

chunks.en: is worth two sela'im,
chunks.st: now worth two sela,

chunks.en: it is brought for his asham,
chunks.st: it shall be sacrificed for his initial guilt offering.

chunks.en: and the second one for his me'ilah,
chunks.st: And with regard to the second ram that he purchased for non-sacred use, if it is now worth two sela, it shall be sacrificed as a guilt offering for his present misuse,

chunks.en: and he brings with it a sela and a fifth.
chunks.st: and he brings with it the sum of one sela and one-fifth to the Temple treasury as payment for his misuse.

summary: A chatas belongs only to the person and the sin it was set aside for. His son cannot bring it, and he cannot use it for a different sin.

chunks.en: One who set aside his chatas
chunks.st: In the case of one who designates a sin offering for his performance of an unwitting sin

chunks.en: and died, his son may not bring it after him.
chunks.st: and dies, his son shall not bring it in his stead,
chunks.stMore: neither on behalf of his father nor for his own unwitting sin, even if it was the same transgression.

chunks.en: And one may not move it from one sin to another sin.
chunks.st: Likewise, one may not bring a sin offering by reassigning it from the sin for which it is designated to atone and sacrificing it for atonement of another sin.

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ עַל חֵלֶב שֶׁאָכַל אֶמֶשׁ לֹא
chunks.en: Even if it was for chelev he ate yesterday,
chunks.st: Even if he designated a sin offering as atonement for forbidden fat that he unwittingly ate yesterday,

chunks.en: he may not bring it for chelev he ate today,
chunks.st: he may not bring it as atonement for forbidden fat that he unwittingly ate today,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 4),
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "his korban for his sin,"
chunks.st: “And he shall bring his sin offering, an unblemished female goat, for his sin that he has sinned” (Leviticus 4:28),

chunks.en: so that his korban must be for that sin.
chunks.st: indicating that he does not satisfy his obligation until his offering is brought for the sake of the sin for which he designated it.

summary: A korban oleh v'yored changes with how rich a person is. If he set aside money for one kind and then became poorer or richer, he may bring a different kind with it.

chunks.en: One may bring, from money set aside for a female lamb,
chunks.st: One may bring a female goat from money consecrated for a sin offering of a female lamb,

words.en: from what was made holy for

chunks.en: a female goat. From money for a female goat,
chunks.st: and a female lamb from money consecrated for a sin offering of a female goat.

words.en: from what was made holy for

chunks.en: a female lamb. From money for a female lamb and a female goat,
chunks.st: And likewise, one may bring doves and pigeons

words.en: from what was made holy for

chunks.en: doves and young pigeons.
chunks.st: from money consecrated for a sin offering of a female lamb and a female goat;

chunks.en: From money for doves and young pigeons,
chunks.st: and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour

words.en: from what was made holy for

chunks.en: a tenth of an eifah of flour.
chunks.st: from money consecrated for a sin offering of doves and pigeons.

words.note: An eifah is a measure; a tenth of it is a small bag of flour.

chunks.en: How so? If he set aside money for a female lamb or a female goat,
chunks.explain: This is a korban oleh v'yored.
chunks.st: How so? If one unwittingly performed a sin for which he is liable to bring a sliding-scale sin offering, which varies based on economic status (see Leviticus 5:1–13; see also 9a), and he designated money to purchase a female lamb or for a female goat

chunks.en: and became poor, he brings a bird.
chunks.st: and then became poorer, he may bring a bird, and the remaining money is non-sacred.

chunks.en: If he became even poorer, he brings a tenth of an eifah.
chunks.st: If he became yet poorer, he may bring one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour.

chunks.en: If he set aside money for a tenth of an eifah,
chunks.st: Likewise, if he designated money to purchase one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour and

chunks.en: and became rich, he brings a bird.
chunks.st: became wealthier, he shall bring a bird.

chunks.en: If he became even richer, he brings a female lamb or a female goat.
chunks.st: If he became yet wealthier, he shall bring a female lamb or a female goat.

chunks.en: If he set aside a female lamb or a female goat and they got a mum,
chunks.st: If one designated a female lamb or goat as an offering and it developed a blemish,
chunks.stMore: he must redeem the animal and bring another offering with the money.

chunks.en: if he wants, he may bring a bird with their money.
chunks.st: If he became poorer, he may bring a bird with its money.

chunks.en: If he set aside a bird and it got a mum,
chunks.st: But if one designated a bird as an offering and it developed a blemish,

chunks.en: he may not bring a tenth of an eifah with its money,
chunks.st: he may not bring one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour with its money,

chunks.en: because a bird cannot be redeemed.
chunks.st: as there is no possibility of redemption for birds.

summary: The Torah sometimes lists sheep before goats, doves before pigeons, and father before mother. Rabbi Shimon shows that both are equal, and the Sages teach whose honor comes first.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: sheep come before goats everywhere in the Torah.
chunks.st: Lambs precede goats almost everywhere
chunks.stMore: in the Torah that they are both mentioned, as in the verse: “You shall take it from the lambs or from the goats” (Exodus 12:5).

chunks.en: You might think it is because they are better than goats.
chunks.st: One might have thought that it is due to the fact that sheep are more select than goats.

chunks.en: So the Torah says (Vayikra 4),
chunks.st: Therefore, the verse states:

chunks.en: "And if he brings a sheep as his korban for a chatas,"
chunks.st: “And he shall bring for his offering a goat” (Leviticus 4:28), after which it is written: “And if he bring a lamb as his offering for a sin offering” (Leviticus 4:32),

chunks.en: which teaches that both of them are equal.
chunks.st: which teaches that both of them are equal.

chunks.he: תּוֹרִין קוֹדְמִין לִבְנֵי יוֹנָה בְכָל מָקוֹם.
chunks.en: Doves come before pigeons everywhere in the Torah.
chunks.st: Similarly, doves precede pigeons almost everywhere
chunks.stMore: in the Torah, as in the verse: “And he shall bring his guilt offering…two doves, or two pigeons” (Leviticus 5:7).

chunks.en: You might think it is because they are better than pigeons.
chunks.st: One might have thought that it is due to the fact that doves are more select than pigeons.

chunks.en: So the Torah says (Vayikra 12),
chunks.st: Therefore, the verse states:

chunks.en: "And a young pigeon or a dove for a chatas,"
chunks.st: “And a pigeon or a dove for a sin offering” (Leviticus 12:6),
chunks.stMore: with the usual order reversed,

chunks.en: which teaches that both of them are equal.
chunks.st: which teaches that both of them are equal.

chunks.en: The father comes before the mother everywhere in the Torah.
chunks.st: Likewise, mention of the father precedes that of the mother almost everywhere
chunks.stMore: in the Torah, as in the verse: “Honor your father and your mother” (Exodus 20:12).

chunks.en: You might think the honor of the father is greater
chunks.st: One might have thought that it is due to the fact that the honor of the father takes precedence over

chunks.en: than the honor of the mother.
chunks.st: the honor of the mother.

chunks.en: So the Torah says (Vayikra 19),
chunks.st: Therefore, the verse states:

chunks.en: "Every man shall fear his mother and his father,"
chunks.st: “Every man shall fear his mother and his father” (Leviticus 19:3),
chunks.stMore: with the order reversed,

chunks.en: which teaches that both of them are equal.
chunks.st: which teaches that both of them are equal.

chunks.en: But the Sages said,
chunks.st: But the Sages said:

chunks.en: the father comes first before the mother everywhere,
chunks.st: Honor of the father takes precedence over honor of the mother everywhere,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּבִין בִּכְבוֹד אָבִיו.
chunks.en: because both he and his mother must honor his father.
chunks.st: due to the fact that both the son and his mother are obligated in the honor of his father.

chunks.en: And also in learning Torah,
chunks.st: And likewise with regard to Torah study,

chunks.en: if the son learned most of his Torah from his rebbi,
chunks.st: if the son was privileged to acquire most of his Torah knowledge from studying before the teacher,

chunks.en: the rebbi comes before the father everywhere,
chunks.st: honor of the teacher takes precedence over honor of the father,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא וְאָבִיו חַיָּבִין בִּכְבוֹד רַבּוֹ:
chunks.en: because both he and his father must honor his rebbi.
chunks.st: due to the fact that both the son and his father are obligated in the honor of his teacher, as everyone is obligated in the honor of Torah scholars.
